Hi Maya — thanks for the questions and for looping Legal. Quick recap below and I attached a short RTBF-runbook with timelines and edge cases. TL;DR: primary data purge ~30 days, backups best-effort purge 90-180 days depending on storage lifecycle; legal holds can delay deletion. Details: 

- Primary data (indexes, object store pointers, application DB): when we receive an authenticated deletion request via API/Console/Support ticket, we schedule an immediate logical purge. Most customer-visible records are removed within 24-72 hours; full background jobs complete within 30 days to sweep caches and dependent indexes.

- Caches & KV stores: ephemeral caches flushed on request; some in-memory state cleared immediately but persistent KV cache entries are removed by the sweep job (included in the 30-day window).

- Backups & snapshots: our default managed snapshot retention is 90 days. Automated backups are on a sliding retention window; we can provide custom retention profiles. When a deletion request is processed we mark the customer dataset for purging; snapshots containing the deleted data are scheduled for deletion at their next waterfall/retention lifecycle point. In practice that means final removal can take up to 90 days under default settings. For blocked/archive backups (e.g., long-term storage) removal may take up to 180 days depending on the underlying provider and immutable snapshot policies.

- Logs & audit trails: we retain structured logs and audit events for 1 year by default (configurable). We can redact personal identifiers from logs on request; fully removing correlated identifiers requires a targeted deletion that may impact traceability. We recommend a redaction-first approach for logs and a separate agreement for full erase if you need audit re-writing.

- Legal hold / subpoenas: if FintechCo instructs us of an active legal hold, we will not delete the held records until the hold is lifted. We surface this as an exception in the RTBF runbook and work with your Legal team on scope.

- Data residency & encryption: data remains in the configured region. We support customer-managed KMS keys for encryption-at-rest, and can operate on dedicated/private deployments if you need stronger residency guarantees.

Next steps / asks from your side:
1) Confirm which data classes you want treated as PII for the purposes of deletion (profile data, transaction text, embeddings, logs).
2) Indicate whether default backup retention (90 days) is acceptable or you need an accelerated purge SLA (we can add to contract).
3) Confirm whether Legal requires a separate addendum for log redaction or legal-hold procedures.

I attached the RTBF runbook PDF and the backup retention table for quick reference. Happy to jump on a 20-min follow-up with Legal if helpful.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi J. and team — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers here and proposed contractual language below; happy to iterate in a quick call.

1) SLA for primary purge: we can commit to a 30-calendar-day purge for primary customer-visible records (indexes, database records, pointers) as a contractual SLA for enterprise customers (can be included in Dedicated/Private plans). We'll add a clause that immediate user-visible removal occurs within 72 hours and full background sweep completes within 30 days.

2) Accelerated backup purge option: yes — we offer an accelerated purge for backups to 60 days as a purchased add-on for regulated accounts. Implementation: mark dataset for expedited deletion and run targeted snapshot lifecycle jobs; note that certain immutable cloud-provider snapshots may still impose a hard minimum (we'll enumerate by provider).

3) Proof of deletion: we can provide an automated signed event (webhook) and a downloadable certificate-of-deletion from the Console when the final purge job completes. The certificate will include timestamps and object ids removed; for backups we will include the retention window and deletion job id.

4) Embeddings and derived artifacts: included — embeddings and model-derived artifacts created from customer-supplied text are in-scope for RTBF and will be marked for purge along with the primary dataset. We will ensure codified behavior in the addendum.

5) Legal holds: exceptions will be documented; when a legal hold is asserted by a customer we will retain the specified dataset until an authorized release is provided by the customer's legal contact. This is an exception to the SLA and will be surfaced as a flagged exception in compliance reports.

Proposed next steps: 
- I'll circulate a 1-page addendum draft that contains the 30-day primary purge SLA, the 60-day accelerated backup option (add-on), proof-of-deletion artifacts, and log redaction options.
- If acceptable, Legal can review and we can lock into the Master Services Agreement / Data Processing Addendum.

Can you confirm whether you want the accelerated backup purge included in the initial contract or as an optional add-on? Also let me know preferred time for a 20-min call tomorrow morning if helpful — slot available 9:30-10:30 PT.
